integrity.label: Original camera file
integrity.explanation: The file has the marks of a camera original from a Generic Camera 1: make and model, original capture time, and manufacturer-specific data (XMP-GCamera), with no image editor recorded. This says where the file comes from, not whether its content is true: metadata can be forged by anyone who knows how.

results.name: Real file format
results.label: Consistent
results.explanation: The extension and the content agree: this is a JPEG file.

results.name: GPS position
results.label: Consistent
results.explanation: Position recorded: 48.85660, 2.35220. Accuracy is not recorded. A recorded position says where the device placed itself, which can be edited like any metadata.

results.explanation: Captured 2025-06-21 13:50:00 (UTC+02:00, from the EXIF offset). No other clock is recorded to compare with.

results.name: Time zone
results.label: Consistent
results.explanation: The device's time zone (UTC+02:00, from the EXIF offset) matches the GPS position, in Europe/Paris.

results.name: Solar consistency
results.label: Consistent
results.explanation: At the place and time recorded in the file (2025-06-21 13:50, time zone from the EXIF offset), the sun was 65° above the horizon, toward the south (179°): full daylight. Outdoor shadows should point north, about 0.5 times as long as the object is tall. The photo shows day, which matches.

results.name: Editing software
results.label: Unverifiable
results.explanation: No software is recorded in the file. Many editors and platforms write nothing, so this neither suggests nor rules out editing.

results.name: C2PA Content Credentials
results.label: Unverifiable
results.explanation: The file carries no Content Credentials (C2PA). Most cameras and phones do not produce them and platforms remove them, so their absence says nothing about the image.

disclaimer: Tala X never certifies that an image is authentic. It reports what can honestly be said about a file. An original camera file is not proof that its content is true: metadata can be forged by anyone who knows how. Tala X is built against platform laundering and recycled images, not against expert forgers.
